    // About

    AI Technical Analyst

    I test AI models, agentic workflows, and MCP servers to separate real capability from theoretical hype.

    I bridge technical architecture with daily execution—building modular, human-in-the-loop automations that simplify complex processes. Whether I’m designing single-page apps or testing multi-agent systems, I stick to one rule: keep the code clean, keep a human in control, and deliver results people can trust.

    Yvonne Martinez

    // My story

    My story.

    It started right at my desk at work, staring down the kind of dense technical documentation that eats up half a day.

    As a Senior Technical Analyst, I kept running into hours lost on searching, reformatting, and digging through noise instead of actually making decisions. I wanted to see if AI could lift that weight without breaking the human process.

    So when I was nominated as our team's AI Champion, I dove right in. Working independently, I automated Oracle SQL reports, built custom financial Gems, and prototyped agentic workflows in Google AI Studio to see what actually stuck. Along the way, I cross-skilled the team, bringing everyone up to speed on what these tools could really do.

    Long before AI tools hit the mainstream, I teamed up with Learning & Development to design learning pathways, build SCORMs in Articulate 360, and create the complete curriculum to launch the very first Pega Chapter at my company.

    That energy powers everything I do now, including aitogethernow.com—built on React, Vite, and Firebase, powered by a FastAPI backend calling Gemini through Vertex AI and MCP. No fluff, just practical tools designed for real utility.

    And I’m keeping that momentum going right now through the Leland AI Builder Program. Working alongside the Leland team and using Claude, I’ve just pushed through nine hands-on builds—ranging from custom voice guides and automated email triage to zero-formula spreadsheet analysis. I build because I love solving real problems, and I build to ship.

    Act 1 · THE PROBLEM

    Great teams, heavy documentation

    Technical teams worked with complex documentation every day. I kept wondering whether AI could lighten it without taking people out of it.

    What I noticed first was how much time went into searching, rewriting and reformatting, and how little into decisions.

    Act 2 · THE CAST

    Me, the teams, and new tools

    Me, the technical teams I supported, and AI tools few of us had tried, starting with Google Gemini and NotebookLM. I raised my hand, and my team nominated me as its AI Champion.

    As Champion, I helped everyone explore a range of AI applications together and find what actually fit their work.

    I had teammates and leaders willing to try something new, and I worked side by side with the people who would use the tools every day.

    Act 3 · THE EXPERIMENT

    Pilot first, then make it fit

    I led pilots for both tools, then kept going. I automated SQL reports in Oracle databases, built financial automation tools with custom Gems, and prototyped in Google AI Studio.

    • Gemini
    • NotebookLM
    • Custom Gems
    • Google AI Studio
    • SQL & Oracle
    Act 4 · THE TURN

    The part nobody planned

    The tools worked best when shaped around real tasks, and people adopted them faster once they saw them save time on their own work. Anything that felt like extra effort got dropped, so I kept every workflow simple.

    Act 5 · WHAT IT CHANGED

    Faster work, with a person still in charge

    Documentation got easier to streamline and tasks moved faster across the teams. One rule the whole way: a person stays in charge.

    Then I taught it. I founded our company’s Pega Chapter and built the curriculum behind it.

    I learned that adoption is a people challenge as much as a technology one. Next time I would bring teams in even earlier and share small wins sooner.

    // How I work

    Human in the loop.

    Three steps, every time.

    The same simple approach on every build, from the first conversation to the finished workflow.

    1

    Understand the people

    I start with the person doing the work, not the tool. What slows them down, and what would they hand off tomorrow?

    2

    Build the workflow

    Small, automated steps connected to the tools they already use, like Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Docs.

    3

    Keep a human in charge

    My assistants draft and suggest. Nothing gets sent or changed until a person has looked at it.

    // Learning

    Certifications and continuous learning.

    I learn the way I teach: hands-on, in small steps, then I share it.

    Two tiers, kept apart

    Exam-certified, and always building.

    From Google Cloud to Pega, my certifications reflect active mastery—backed by verified credentials, exact dates, and hands-on application.

    What changed in how I work
    • Claude reads my context first. CLAUDE.md holds my role, answer style and standing rules, so I no longer re-explain them each session.
    • My drafts follow a written voice. guides/email-voice-guide.md came from 20 of my sent emails, and every draft is checked against its calibration tests.
    • Every claim gets a source check. session-4-data/research-notes.md lists each slide claim next to its source and the result of checking it.
    My strongest build

    Spreadsheet Analysis is my strongest build because it is the most checked. session-3-data/college-analysis.xlsx covers 200 schools, with live formulas and a source on every row. It showed that an 8.5x tuition gap between two schools came with a 31% gap in ten-year median earnings (s3-notes.md). The notes in session-3-data/research-notes.md record a recalculation of all 1,994 formula cells with no mismatches, and the finding shipped as a 14-slide deck.

    What I am building next

    Next is the Zumba Practice & Routine Planner, a weekly scheduled task I have scoped. It sits in What I'm Automating Next with three more ideas.
